newsitem.title: TURKEY: Kurd guerrillas kill three Turkish teachers.
newsitem.headline: Kurd guerrillas kill three Turkish teachers.

text.p: Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebels killed three Turkish teachers in the southeastern province of Diyarbakir on Tuesday, security officials said.

They said a group of rebels abducted six teachers from their homes in the village of Hantepe in the early hours of the morning, took them to the countryside 10 km (six miles) away and shot three of them dead. They released the other three, the officials told Reuters.

Two of the dead were a married couple, the officials said. Amnesty International said in a report released on Tuesday that the rebels have killed 90 teachers since they took up arms for Kurdish self rule in 1984. More than 20,000 people have died in the conflict.
The attack came just over a week after children in Turkey returned to school following the summer break. The rebels have not killed any teachers for more than a year.
Turkey has blamed rebel commander Semdin Sakik, believed to have come to the Diyarbakir area from northern Iraq in the last month, for previous attacks on teachers.
The rebels say they target educators because they symbolise the forced assmiliation of Kurdish children into Turkish culture. The teaching of Kurdish is forbidden in Turkish schools.
